output: Scientific Hypothesis: In the context of the National Longitudinal Survey of Youth (NLSY79) dataset, there is no significant relationship between time preference indicators (measured by DISSAVED and SAMESAVE) and BMI in Hispanic men. This hypothesis is derived from the analysis of the dataset, where correlation coefficients were found to be very weak (r ≈ 0.004 for DISSAVED and r ≈ 0.106 for SAMESAVE), and regression analysis showed that these variables do not significantly predict BMI (p-values of 0.992 for DISSAVED and 0.354 for SAMESAVE). Therefore, time preference does not appear to have a statistically significant impact on BMI in Hispanic men based on this dataset.
